title: feat(spec): FLOW_FAILED carries the refused write's inner refusal — AutomationResult.userMessage / innerRefusal and one FlowFailureDetailsSchema for the four doors
body:
Closes #24996

Clause-②: yes (widening)

The contract half of ruling **B′** on #24914: the maintainer's 「同意」 in decision batch #379, item 5. With it, the refusal a flow write node meets reaches the client structurally, the way a record save's refusal does. This PR changes only `packages/spec`, plus one runtime docblock (named below). Emission is #24914's job: the crud nodes, the engine carriage and the four doors. The console half is an objectui card. Until those land, nothing on the wire changes.

## The ruling's bullets (verbatim from #24996, "What the ruling binds")

> - `AutomationResult` (`packages/spec/src/automation/flow.zod.ts`, beside `successMessage` / `errorMessage` :1085–1086) gains an optional `userMessage` with `ApiErrorSchema`'s semantics (`packages/spec/src/api/contract.zod.ts:50-97`: producer-marked end-user text that "never replaces message") and an optional inner-refusal member of shape `{ code, message }`, `code` in its wire spelling. The member's name is the spec seat's; its shape is ruled.
> - The `FLOW_FAILED` details of the trigger, resume, `/actions` and endpoint doors declare that member ONCE (the `ResumeFailureDetailsSchema` pattern, `packages/spec/src/api/automation-api.zod.ts:430`), so the four doors emit one shape. `message` is unchanged everywhere: no wording pin moves.
> - `AutomationResult.code` stays a closed union (#9378 ruling `5321043983`): no new ledger code; the inner code rides inside the member.
> - ⛔ Not this card: the crud-node and engine changes (#24914), the doors' emission (#24914, cli cross-lane), the console (objectui), the unique sentence's object API name (#24951, engine).

## What changed

- **`AutomationResult`** (`packages/spec/src/contracts/automation-service.ts`) gains two optional members:
  - `userMessage?: string`, with exactly `ApiErrorSchema.userMessage`'s semantics: presence IS the marking, it is set only when the inner refusal's producer opted in, and it never replaces `error`;
  - `innerRefusal?: FlowInnerRefusal`.
- **`TriggerFlowResponseSchema.data`** mirrors both members. The compile-time pin `TriggerFlowResponse['data']` = `AutomationResult` (#13078) holds.
- **`FlowInnerRefusalSchema`** (new, `@objectstack/spec/api`) is `{ code, message }`, with `code: ErrorCode`. `ErrorCode` is the same closed ADR-0112 set that `ApiErrorSchema.code` parses against, so "wire spelling" is enforced, not just described: `UNIQUE_VIOLATION` parses, and a driver spelling such as `ER_DUP_ENTRY` is refused.
- **`FlowFailureDetailsSchema`** (new) is the `error.details` of every door's `400 FLOW_FAILED` arm, declared once: `errorMessage?`, `summary?` and `innerRefusal?`. It is a plain non-strict object, the `ResumeFailureDetailsSchema` pattern. On the resume door, `runId` / `status` / `repairable` sit beside these keys in the same object, and each schema parses its own members.
- **The #9585 ceiling.** On `/actions`, `error.details` was capped at "exactly two keys … no new schema keys". The ruling relaxes that cap by one named key: the declared set is now the three keys above, at all four doors. The ceiling is enforced in runtime, not in spec:
  - the `FlowActionRunDetails` docblock (`packages/runtime/src/action-execution.ts`), which this PR updates to cite ruling B′ (comment only, no type change);
  - the exact-equality negative pin in `packages/runtime/src/actions-flow-dispatch-status.test.ts`. That pin is **left unchanged on purpose**: nothing emits `innerRefusal` yet, so it still describes the wire exactly. #24914 relaxes it in the same change that emits the key.
- **Unchanged:** `error.message` at every door, `error.code: FLOW_FAILED`, and `AutomationResult.code` (still the closed union, no new ledger code). No wording pin moves.
- **Regenerated with repo tooling** (`check:generated --fix`, which rewrote only what it proved stale): `api-surface/`, `export-origins/`, `declaration-map/`, `authorable-surface/`, `json-schema.manifest/`, `content/docs/references/**`, and the strictness-ledger counts (`api/` 446 → 448, the two new object sites).

## The member's name: `innerRefusal`

- It uses the ruling's own words ("the inner refusal").
- It fits the vocabulary that already exists around flow failures, where "refusal" is the word for a classified no: `FlowActionRefusal`, `classifyFlowRefusal`, `FlowRefusalCode`, `refusal: true` on `ApiErrorSchema`.
- The `inner` prefix keeps it distinct from `refusalMessage`, which belongs to an `end` node's deliberate `outcome: 'refused'`, a different thing.
- Rejected alternatives:
  - `cause`: it collides with `Error.cause` chaining semantics and says nothing about the shape;
  - `writeRefusal`: too narrow, since the same `{ code, message }` shape fits a read node refused by permission;
  - `error`: already the diagnostic string on `AutomationResult`.

## Contract review owed

This PR owes a **`CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`** contract review: `Clause-②: yes (widening)`, a new public schema pair, and a ruled relaxation of the #9585 ceiling. Two choices are left to the reviewer explicitly:

1. `innerRefusal.code` is the closed `ErrorCode`, not an open string. A producer must map to the wire spelling, and an app-specific hook code has no `declaredCode` arm inside the member.
2. `FlowFailureDetailsSchema` declares the two existing artefacts (`errorMessage`, `summary`) beside the new key, so the ceiling is a declared set instead of prose. Before this PR, those artefacts existed on the wire but were not declared in spec.

## Tests

- `packages/spec/src/api/automation-api.zod.test.ts`, new suite `FlowFailureDetailsSchema — one inner-refusal shape across the four FLOW_FAILED doors`:
  - for each of the four doors (trigger, resume, `/actions`, endpoint), an envelope whose `details.innerRefusal` is `{ code: 'UNIQUE_VIOLATION', message }` and which has a top-level `userMessage` validates through `BaseResponseSchema` and `FlowFailureDetailsSchema`. On the resume door it also validates through `ResumeFailureDetailsSchema`;
  - the same four envelopes without either member still validate;
  - the declared key set is exactly the three ruled keys;
  - an unregistered inner code is refused at `['code']`;
  - both members of the inner refusal are required;
  - the trigger response data accepts the mirrored members.
- A type-level pin, `FlowFailureInnerRefusalIsTheContracts`, holds `FlowFailureDetails['innerRefusal']` equal to `AutomationResult['innerRefusal']`.

Local results, all at `22786c992e` (`git rev-parse --short HEAD`, the final commit):

- `pnpm --filter @objectstack/spec test`: 703 files / 21382 passed, 1 todo.
- `pnpm --filter @objectstack/spec test:repo`: 72 files / 1236 passed.
- `pnpm --filter @objectstack/spec typecheck`: exit 0. That covers `tsc --noEmit`, the scripts typecheck and the test-typecheck ratchet, which compiles the new type-level pin.
- `pnpm --filter @objectstack/spec check:generated --fix`: 5 artifacts were proven stale and regenerated, then re-checked green.
- The runtime ceiling pin, `actions-flow-dispatch-status.test.ts`: 19 passed, unchanged, as expected.
- `runtime` `tsc --noEmit`: exit 0.
- `node scripts/pm/dispatch-gates.mjs --commands` derived 113 commands, plus the 6 roster families that sit under a touched directory. 118 of these 119 are exit 0. A first pass printed PREREQUISITE NOT MET for six of them; those were re-run green after the dependency closure was built. `check:dual-build-cjs-loads` is **NOT MEASURED**: it needs a full workspace build and is left to CI's `Build Core`.
- `pnpm lint` (repo-wide eslint) was not run locally and is CI's.

## Acceptance notes

- **Premise correction.** The issue places `AutomationResult` in `packages/spec/src/automation/flow.zod.ts` :1085. Those lines are `FlowSchema`'s authored `successMessage` / `errorMessage`, which are flow-definition keys. `AutomationResult` is the TypeScript interface in `packages/spec/src/contracts/automation-service.ts`, and its Zod mirror is `TriggerFlowResponseSchema.data`. The members land there, and `flow.zod.ts` is untouched: a runtime-produced `userMessage` is not something a flow author writes. The claim's file surface named `flow.zod.ts`, so `contracts/automation-service.ts` (and the one runtime docblock) are additions to that surface, declared here.
- `pnpm --filter @objectstack/runtime typecheck` is exit 1 locally, in its `check:test-typecheck` half only. It reports one type error in `src/organization-ownership-boot-guard.turso-remote.kernel.test.ts`, a file this PR does not touch. This PR's runtime diff is a docblock-only edit, so it cannot move a type verdict. The cause is unverified: possibly a stale dependency `dist` on this shared box, possibly drift already on main. CI's `TypeScript Type Check` is the authority on it.
- `contract.zod.ts` is untouched: the #9585 ceiling does not live there. `ApiErrorSchema.userMessage` already carries the envelope's top-level channel.
